utterances.text: Leopold Kaufer did not leave town. He stayed in town and he died in town. As for the rest, they followed you to Pale, because you probably brought pressure to bear, in that sense. So they all left us. No one was trying to get rid of them. They left of their own accord.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mrs. Fatima, I understand your emotions, but if you are saying that I exerted pressure on them, then I will have to spend a lot of time proving that that is not true. You will agree that I am not a magician so that I could lure 250 doctors to leave Sarajevo; right?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: No, you're not, but that's what your policy was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Well, now, did they flee from your policy or did they run towards my policy? That is a case that has to be proven. Do you remember that Professor Surgeon Borisa Starovic was also a victim of sniper fire?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't know, but I know that he was ill and that because of his illness he left. That's what he had said anyway.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: However, that was so well known, and as a matter of fact, he was even forced to say that he was the victim of Serb fire, although Serbs were not firing anywhere nearby, but never mind, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you something. Please don't bother me with all of that, who left, why they left, et cetera. I came here to say how many children and civilians you targeted with your army, as if they were balls or objects down there. That's what I came to say. Believe me, they all know why they left the city, but that's not what I came to talk about here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I believe that I do have the right to ask you everything that you knew about and everything that you had touched upon. You said that we were shelling, and you said that we were shelling all of the city, although you couldn't see that, so please don't get angry. I have to illuminate all of these matters. Nothing should remain unclear. This is a criminal court. This is not a debate club. So we have to clarify everything. We have to see whether you know something or whether you had heard of other things, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exactly as you said. This is not a debate club. Just ask questions, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope, Excellency, that you are going to protect me. If you don't protect me then I have to say this, because I cannot accept the limit that the witness is imposing on me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we do protect you, as long as you are asking relevant questions. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mrs. Zaimovic, you said in your statement of the 18th of January, 2002, in the Galic case, on page 1851, in paragraph 25, that one morning you were sitting on the balcony and you heard an explosion. Then you said that that was a barrel that had been full of explosive material and was then pushed downhill, and it ultimately destroyed some houses. You said the same thing on the next page, in paragraph 1, as well. And then you said that there were only civilian targets there and that there were no military targets in sight; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said. As for military and civilian targets, I said what I said because I saw barrels hitting houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did you just come to the conclusion that it was a barrel because you heard the explosion?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: We heard the explosion and we saw the barrels moving down from that rock.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: One barrel or several barrels?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Several barrels.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You, therefore, think and say that there were no military installations or targets over there.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I have no knowledge or awareness of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now in the hospital, there were no soldiers or military installations or artillery or mortars or anything of that sort; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And Breka didn't have any military units or military installations; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, no, it didn't.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we now have a map displayed, please. It is 1D906. May we have it called up on e-court. 1D906 is the document number. And may I ask the Registrar to provide Mrs. Zaimovic with a marker so that she can draw on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Have they provided you with a pen, Mrs. Zaimovic?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Would you now mark in on the map where your building was within the hospital compound.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you know that the children's surgery ward was to be found at the central entrance to the hospital, which is here. Kosevo Hospital, this is the central part, as far as I know. This map is a little different than the one I was looking at just a moment ago, but I think it's somewhere in that general area.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. That is the -- those are the surgical clinics; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Now do you know what is to be found underneath Stjepan Tomic street? Which faculties are there there?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: The medical faculty is lower down and the electrical engineering factory.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Just underneath the street, Stjepan Tomic street. Which faculty buildings are there there?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: The electrical engineering faculty, as far as I know, was located in that area. That was the only one. I don't know of any others. And the faculty of architecture. That was in the same building.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Would you mark that on the map for us.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I'll do my best. I'm not quite sure that I'm getting it right because I'm not a military expert. And I apologise. I worked at the clinic, so I never gave maps and the like any thought.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Very well. But we all know that's where the faculty buildings were. Now, if you look at -- in the upper right-hand corner, 901 is the elevation point, you have the hill there. Meta [phoen] hill. Would you mark that in for us.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I can't see that. I don't know. You mean above Breka?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: About the -- above the forests, the Sedam Suma forest. The upper right-hand corner where it says Grdonj. 901, elevation 901.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Is this what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And who here had control of Grdonj, madam?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You don't know that it was the Muslim units who were up at Grdonj?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't. I'm not a military expert, as I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, could you mark in Betanija? Do you see where it says Betanija in the upper left-hand corner? Is that where the obstetrician ward and maternity ward was?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Where it says Djecija, yes. Betanija over here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, could you indicate where you, yourself, lived?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Breka. I lived right above the hospital, in that general area.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The second row of houses; right?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the second row of houses and you know that full well. You know where that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now do you see the entrance to the tunnel? It says Kosevsko Brdo, Kosevo hill, Kosevsko Brdo. And you can see the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: You mean over here, Kosevsko Brdo?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, it's the stadium, but it says Kosevsko Brdo, Gorica, so somewhere in the middle, to the left of the map in the middle.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I can't see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It's written up in large letters. Right along the left-hand side of the map.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: It says Jezero and it says Djecija. But why are you asking me all this? Why are you asking me to indicate things on this map? I'm not a military expert. Could you -- Your Honours, I don't want to answer questions like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mrs. Zaimovic, he's entitled to ask questions, and he wants the Judges to be familiar with the geography, as we are not familiar with it. So during the course of examination and question and answers, we get familiarised with the maps. I see Kosevsko Brdo in the left part underneath Kosevo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really can't see it. Kosevo is over here. I can see that. I can't see Kosevsko Brdo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: To the left could you see Kosevo there. Do you see Crni Vrh there in the left part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. You mean this here. There's Kosevsko Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, right above where it says Kosevsko Brdo, do you see the entrance to the tunnel there?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the red, the area in red?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, within the circle. You've already drawn a circle around Kosevsko Brdo, and you see right above that that's where it is.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. That's right.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: And that leads directly to the hospital. There's the bypass passing over the cemetery and leading on towards the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Now what about Breka Potok or Breka stream? Where is that? Can you pinpoint that for us, please?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Is it on the map?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No. There's Breka and then --

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Breka Potok moves towards Pionirska street. It's in that general area. Somewhere over here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do you know where the institute for the deaf and dumb, deaf and dumb children is, called Nemanja Vlatkovic?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could you mark that in?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: That's near Breka too, somewhere above the end part of the hospital compound. So somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know where the bakery at Breka is?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: The bakery? I don't know where the bakery is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Madam Zaimovic, if we could put D for the institute for the deaf and dumb in order for us to remember later on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Now these two circles where you lived. You lived by the lower circle; right, where it says 201?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Over here. Right up above the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Thank you. Now, may I ask you to sign that, put your initials on the map, and I'd like to tender this map into evidence now, please, having recorded that.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Do you want me to write the date as well?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Well, that would be good -- a good idea.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be admitted as?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D120, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. We will probably come back to this map later on, but may we have called up another document now which is 1D905, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And while we're waiting for that, let me tell you what the document is about. It's a document from the General Staff of the BH Army, the command of the 1st Corps, and you know that the 1st Corps was in Sarajevo, don't you?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Here organisational changes are being ordered -- or, rather, the General Staff is ordering organisational changes in the area of responsibility of the 1st Corps.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ah, we haven't got it on our screens yet. May this document be called up on e-court, please. And may we have both the English and Serbian version on the screen, please, so that Mrs. Zaimovic can see what it's about. So both versions, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And on the first page in that first rectangle, we see in the area of responsibility of the 1st Corps formed the following battle units, the command of the 12th Division with the staff units and headquarters in Sarajevo, and the following units will comprise the composition of the division of 105th Mountain Brigade. There was 105th Motorised Brigade, and now here we have the 105th Mountain Brigade. Have you heard of that?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I have, but this has got nothing to do with why I have come in here to this courtroom to testify. I wasn't a military expert. I worked at the clinic all my life and the whole time, and I wasn't interested in military units or their names or numbers or whatever. So I -- my answer is that I have no knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Was your son in the army?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, my son was in the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In what unit?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: The 105th.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And you weren't interested in the 105th Brigade at all?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: He had to go. He was recruited and had to join up and, of course, defend his country.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Madam, that is commendable, but how is it possible that you're not interested in the 105th Brigade of which your son was a member? Where was the brigade deployed?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know that. I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You don't know that it's area of responsibility was Breka?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now let's move on to page 3 of this same document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May that be displayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that rectangle there, the Motorised Brigades of the 1st Corps should be restructured to become mountain brigades as a provisional military formation, number T412.194, and it involves 105th, 102nd, and 105th Brigade should become the 105th Mountain Brigade which was your son's brigade; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, most probably, but I really can't say. I don't know. What was important to me was to have my son come back home alive.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Certainly, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now may we see the last page of this document. It is army General Rasim Delic who signed the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is that Rasim Delic's signature? Is that what it says there?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it says Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender 1D905 into evidence, please. And may we have 1D902 next.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Unless it is objected to, it will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do object to this document. She hasn't been able to speak to any of it. For that reason, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your ground of objection is based upon the relevance or the authenticity?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The relevance, Your Honour. And we don't know about the authenticity because she hasn't been able to speak to the document at all. She doesn't recognise the document. She hasn't said that that's Delic's signature. She simply said that the word "Delic" is there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber does not find much relevance of this document as such. You will have another opportunity to tender this document. On that ground this will not be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I see the relevance with respect to the witness's credibility, first and foremost, and the fact that I want to prove and show that Sarajevo was a fortress and fulcrum, a military stronghold, and not a peaceful town that was attacked by some wild men. And to be quite honest, I'm surprised that this document is not going to be admitted. But let's have 1D902 next, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is the command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, dated the 25th of February, 1995, and it is a report sent by the intelligence services to what it says at the bottom. We see that the 102nd Motorised Brigade or Mountain Brigade and the 105th Mountain Brigade is referred to. Now let's move on to page 5, please, of this same document. Madam, do you know where Trampina street is?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I can't really remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know where the Ivan Cankar school is?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember that either.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know where Hladivode is?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know where Kobilja Glava is?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I know where Kobilja Glava is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mala Kula?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: What Mala Kula?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Well there is just one Mala Kula, and I think that you can see it on that map. It's above Breka where you were. Let's see now what it says in relation to the 105th Brigade. Commander Izet Berkovic, have you heard of him? Do you know of him?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What about Tinjak, Mustafa?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Salko Softic?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Ah-ah. Now, do you see that it says here that the command post is in the Sipad building in Trampina street and the auxiliary command post is in the Ivan Cankar school; isn't that what is written here?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I am no military expert. I am asking you very nicely not to ask me about things like this. I spent all the time with the children at the clinic. I have no idea about this. This means nothing to me. You're putting questions to me that I know nothing of. Please don't put military questions to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Well, see, Ms. Zaimovic, it says here number of men 5.500 to 6.000. That's the number of soldiers that are in your neighbourhood and around your neighbourhood with all of the necessary infrastructure, logistics, with a rear command post, and you are saying that there was nothing there and that you don't know anything about it? And your own son is on that unit.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: That's your reports. I have no idea about any of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, can Mr. Karadzic put a question and not comment when he's speaking with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What do you see as comments?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What is his question to the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Was his question not whether she knows that 5.000 or 6.000 number of soldiers were in her neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I got up in the middle of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mrs. Zaimovic, may I read this out to you, the zone of responsibility of this brigade, the 105th Brigade, the brigade that your son was in, Hladivode, Mala Kula, Breka, Potok, Pionirska Dolina, Kobilja Glava, composition five battalions including the rear, and so on and so forth, the number of personnel is between 5.500 to 6.000 men. At Srebrenik, that's where the command post of the 1st Battalion is. Hladivode, Mala Kula is the area. The second one is commanded by Senad Tokaca, and the command is at the institute of seismology, do you know that that institute is there?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that battalion had about 1.000 men. The 3rd Battalion is commanded by Enver Krljus. The command is in a day care centre at Kosevsko Brdo. The defense area is Breka Potok, Sipska Kosa. The 4th Battalion, the commander is a certain Daidza. Manoeuvre Battalion, it only consists of Muslims under the age of 30. Engineer battalion, the command is in Razija Omanovic elementary school. Do you know where that school is?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I do know, but for heaven's sake, I have no idea about any of this. I have no idea about any of this. You have to realise that I don't know anything about that. You know that. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But you see that it is written here that that's where the command posts are, in day care centres, kindergartens, schools, and your son is fighting in that same unit. They are in uniform. They are passing by there, and you do not know anything about this very strong unit consisting of 6.000 men, a brigade, a proper brigade that is guarding your own neighbourhood, and you are trying to say that you don't know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What's the population of Breka?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that either. I don't know exactly. I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Well, I'll tell you. Not more than 2- or 3.000. And the number of soldiers is double in relation to that; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: That's what you're saying. I don't speak about that and I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellencies, I am tendering this document. I believe that it is more than relevant because the place was full of soldiers. It was teeming with soldiers. It is more than relevant, not only in terms of the credibility of this witness but also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No speech, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, let's look at it. It falls into two categories. You have information from documents that you can use to base cross-examination on. For instance, you have a document which says, As far as the 105th Motorised Brigade is concerned, in the vicinity we're talking about, there were between 5.500 and 6.000 men. So it's perfectly legitimate for you to ask the witness, Were you aware that in that area of responsibility there were up to 6.000 soldiers. There's no problem with that. It becomes a perfectly legitimate question, but, of course, you are bound by the answer the witness gives. But that doesn't prove the document. Unless this witness was either the author or recipient or otherwise had personal knowledge of the document, it doesn't prove the document. It didn't prevent you from using the context of the document to ask questions in cross-examination, and it doesn't prevent you from proving the document in due course as part of the Defence case. But unless the witness can speak to, identify, or accept the document as genuine, that's a completely separate issue as to the use of the document as a basis for cross-examination. Do you see the distinction? I see that Mr. Robinson does.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I do very much, Judge Morrison, but I'm wondering whether that's not consistent with the practice that we've adopted so far in this trial because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's the point I'm going to take. Ms. Sutherland, apart from the principles set out by His Honour Judge Morrison, has it not been our practice that as regards the military documents or official documents, has it not been our practice to admit -- admit them as far as the authenticity of those were not challenged? Or Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If you would just give me a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'd say that's -- I'd have to canvass -- excuse me, Your Honour, canvass all the specific rulings, but I say generally that's probably been the case. I would -- and -- so I understand the Court's point in that respect. I would note that I received an e-mail from Mr. Robinson recently in connection with the proposed submission I had, suggesting an approach to documents that was not consistent with the one he's advancing now. So we're just looking for some consistency. I would note, as I have on previous occasions, that in a circumstance like this, when the witness indicates quite clearly that he or she doesn't know about that particular document, the submission is basically in the form of a bar table or an independent submission. I don't particularly have a problem with that. I think that can indeed advance the relevant information available to the Chamber, but it obviously can't be a one-sided affair or the Court won't have the benefit of the information it needs. So to the extent it's considered a practice, then we'll certainly be doing the same. I don't want to resile from the fact that I have encouraged, on a number of occasions, the Court to receive documents that the particular witness may not have authored or specifically received but about which the provenance is reasonably known and the reliability is reasonably clear. So I certainly don't want the Prosecution to be adopting two different positions, but that would apply equally to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If we are talking about a statement, a witness statement given -- bear with us, Madam Zaimovic. We are having some digression now. If we are dealing with witness statement or paper -- newspaper clippings, I see a point. Unless the witness confirms the content or the veracity of the document, we cannot admit those documents. However, in terms of official documents, military documents, if we start -- parties start asking the parties to authenticating such documents, there will be no end to --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No. And I'm reminded of the Court's ruling, which I believe was on the last court date or the date before, in which you said precisely that in connection with the tendering of excerpts from larger documents which were official, contemporaneous documents. I see that is, indeed, consistent with the practice that you just asked about, and so I guess to that extent, and I think it's a clear signal from the Court, the answer to your question, Your Honour, is yes, that is the practice the Court seems to have adopted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Ms. Sutherland. I haven't asked what your position is about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, again, I think in fairness, since I've just responded to the general question, I'm not going to suggest that this document somehow falls outside the parameters of that response, and I believe that's what the Court was -- why the Court made the inquiry in the first place. So you've heard our response the general proposition that you made in connection with the practice, and I'm not -- not in a position to challenge the provenance of this document. It appears to be an official document. I do want to point out that we are receiving the documents almost as you see them on the screen yourself, and we really don't have -- I mean, some of these may, in fact, be on the Prosecution's 65 ter list. Some of them may be easily -- for some of them the provenance may be easily identified. For others, there may be more questions. It may result in requests for -- that the documents be marked for identification so we can check that because of the rapid timing, but -- so there's a difference between indicating that we're not in a position to know precisely the provenance of a document at the particular moment it's tendered and objecting to the document because we think it's unreliable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So are you minded to reconsider your response given to the previous document?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, in light of the guidance -- the practice the Court has identified, the guidance it's providing and with the caveat there may be numbers of documents for which we would seek an opportunity to consider the provenance after it's marked for identification, the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, if you could remind me of the 65 ter number of the document we just dealt with. The second one, which is before us now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 903 -- no, no. 903, the new one. 905, actually. No. No. This was 902. 902. The last one was 902, the one that we dealt with. 902. 1D902.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. The Chamber by majority, Judge Morrison dissenting, finds this document relevant in terms of the credibility of the witness and the -- and as far as authenticity is concerned, following the practice of the Tribunal, admits the document, which is 1D902, and reconsider the previous decision regarding 1D905 and admits that document as well. What will be the exhibit numbers?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 905 will be D121, and 1D902 will be Exhibit D122.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. May I have 1D906 called up again, please. And I'd like Mrs. Zaimovic to be provided with a pencil. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, Mrs. Zaimovic, would you indicate Kosevo stadium, please. We all know where it is.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: You set fire to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now indicate Bjelave, please.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you now indicate the Centrotrans settlement?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know where that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I think it's between Kosevo and Pionirska street. You remember where the Centrotrans district was?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Never mind, never mind. Now, could you sign the map and then I'd like to tender it into evidence. And we'll identify the Centrotrans settlement in due course, on another occasion.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Now 1D903 is the next document I'd like us to look at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the annotated map will be Exhibit D123.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D903 next, please. 1D903. Thank you. Only the relevant portions have been translated, but we have nothing against the Registrar having it all translated. This is a document dated the 13th of August, 1995, providing intelligence about the enemy in the area of responsibility of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. May we move on to page 4, please. No, page 5. Page 5 of that same document. The passage that has been highlighted, which has been translated by the way. It says here that the 105th Mountain Brigade has around 5.000 soldiers divided into four battalions, of which one is constantly at Niska plateau. The area of responsibility of this brigade is Sijanicka Kosa, Pionirska Dolina, Grdonj, Hladivode. Supporting assets, a battery of 120-millimetre mortars at the Centrotrans neighbourhood, a battery of 82-millimetre mortars at the Kosevo stadium, and two howitzers of 105 millimetres located at Bjelovar. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I see that it says that there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did your son every talk to you about any of that?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, I'd like to tender this document as well. That's another passage on the following page but that's not important. Anyway, I'd like to tender this into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. Since I started taking these. It's not fully translated. That's another reason for the MFI request. It's also extremely difficult to read the B/C/S we have here, which would be another basis for asking that this be MFI'd at the moment, so we can either seek a better copy or make further inquiries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll marked it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D124, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May we have the map again, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sorry. If it is convenient, we can have a second break.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Excellency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will have a break for 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Ms. Zaimovic, did you work every day?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, every day.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And how much time did you spend at work?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it depended. Mostly from morning till evening. Sometimes I had to stay on during the night, too, because the nurses that live far away were not able to come to work because of the shelling.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And who was the head nurse before you?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Before me it was a nun. Her name was Sergeja.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And what happened to her?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: She retired.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, can we have the map displayed again, please, the same map, Your Excellency, so that we don't have to have a new drawing and a new exhibit every time. So D123, the map that we were previously looking at, please. Well, I can tender it into evidence, but then I'll be tendering a new map with the new markings. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, Mrs. Zaimovic, do you have a pencil? And if you do, could you mark in the area of Ciglane.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. And now could you draw a circle around the blue skyscraper, "plavi solitar" [phoen].

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Which blue skyscraper?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Well, everybody from Sarajevo knows what is meant by the blue skyscraper. By the cemetery and the tunnel leading to the hospital. You know where the blue skyscraper was.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the two blue skyscrapers opposite the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Right. The two blue skyscrapers opposite the hospital. Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's right.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they're somewhere in this area here. Thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, that's Breka. But underneath the faculty building. You remember the blue skyscraper with the cafe and everything. Right opposite the cemetery and by the faculty building. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I do vaguely remember, but I can't remember well enough to mark it in here. And it's not important, after all. I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, may we have document 1D920. It hasn't been translated. Yes. Can we have this recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, do you have the large bundle of photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't taken the binder with me, but I know that it does exist, the bundle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: It's just that I see on one of the photographs a blue skyscraper, and I'm just wondering if that's the one you're referring to. It's on the photograph that looks like that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Excellency, that's it. That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like to tender this map marked separately from the previous one? Yes. Can we save it separately --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit D125.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now, may we have 1D920, 920. It hasn't been translated yet, that is, but I'm just going to read two or three lines from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And while we're waiting, madam, have you heard had of Juka Prazina?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know that he became a general in the war?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know that he was a well-known criminal prior to that?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that either. I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And who was Juka Prazina?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I heard that he had taken part in the defence of the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: When he was wounded just prior to the war, was he treated at Kosevo Hospital?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. He was an adult patient, and adult patients didn't come to our children's ward, children's clinic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like you to focus on paragraphs 4 and 5 of this document. It says: "Juka Prazina's headquarters is located in Ciglane, at the intersection towards the hospital in the blue high-rise building. They interrogate prisoner in the theatre building in the city centre." Did you know that Juka Prazina had his headquarters so near to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender 1D920, please, and we will be providing -- oh, I see. It has been translated. I didn't realise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour, although I would note that the stamp hasn't been translated. It's not a full translation, but -- so it can either be MFI'd until the document's properly translated or it can be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Mark for identification pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D126, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So I note that this is a draft translation by the Defence teams. So we will wait for the official translation. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May I have 1D921 next, please, 921. Yes, the document is on our screens. I am not sure whether it's been translated yet. I don't think so. It says Ministry of the Interior, National Security Service, Republika Srpska, the War Department of Ilidza. Now, may we have page 2 of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Madam, did you know that most of the fighting in Sarajevo was started by the BH Army? Almost all the battles were started by the BH Army. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: No. All I know is that you shot from up on the hill and that you targeted the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: All right. We'll come to that. But you didn't know, you say, that all the offensives that were launched in Sarajevo were launched by the BH Army. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: How is that possible when it was on television, the information was broadcast over television? The people were told what positions they had taken control of and where they broke through, and so on.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I was at the clinic. There was no electricity or water. The children were wounded. We didn't know where to turn first, we had so much work to do. We worked from morning to night. And when I went home, I was so tired and I didn't even have any food to cook for the children. My life during the war was very difficult, and I don't know about anything of the things you're asking me about, and I'm not interested in them. I have to be quite sincere there. You're asking me about military matters, something that you should ask military experts and not me. I have come here to testify about the difficulties that the children were facing, children who were wounded and who were killed, whose parents were crying, whose lives were disrupted and were targeted like pigeons in town. Of that's what I want to say. Do you have any conscience? Do you have a conscience, because you destroyed the Muslim children and the Croatian children and the Serbian children. That's what you did. You destroyed them all. That's what I've come here to talk about and not to speak about military strategy that I know nothing whatsoever about.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, madam, but as soon as you say that somebody shot, you provide the basis for me to ask you why and how. As soon as you're saying that Breka was shelled, I had to put it to you that your son was a member of the 105th Brigade which numbered 6.000 men and that the whole place was teeming with soldiers, that there were more soldiers than the inhabitants of Breka.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Leave my son alone. That's not true and leave my son alone. I'm not talking about your children. I don't want us to talk about our children. We're discussing something quite different here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Madam, I have every respect for your husband who was a friend of mine and your child, and it was his duty to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Come to your questions. You haven't cross-examined yet the evidence which was given by this witness. Let's move on to your real topic, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We'll come back to this document. 1D946 is the next one I'd like us to look at. It has been translated, so may we have both versions, the Serbian and English on our screens. Can we have a split screen, please? Thank you. It says, "Military secret, highly confidential." The date is the 28th of July, 1993, an interim combat report for the 28th of July, 1993. It says: "Today the enemy has violated the cease-fire to the Serb side. His firing positions, mortar located in the Kosevo Hospital compound. They fired 20, 82-millimetre mines on the Jagomir ground and Ernest Grin." Do you know where those are?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: "The mines were falling in the region of Promolj, and the head of the hospital, Cukovic, Miladin, was killed as a result and a nurse wounded. The snipers are constantly active and a soldier from the Rajlovac Barracks was killed by sniper fire. Engineering works are still underway, and PANs and PATs are being used and pound the lines of the division with the Ilijas Brigade." So within the hospital compound, you had several mortars, 82-millimetre ones, and 20 mines, and you say you know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Probably that's not -- that's not true, and I really don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Well, this is a secret document, highly confidential.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It wasn't intended for any propaganda purposes, but I'd like to tender the document into evidence now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While we have admitted so far such documents, I -- I'm wondering what's the -- what's the point of your tendering all these documents with the witness. Are you not minded to call a witness who can speak about these documents?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Excellency, the witness provided me with the basis for me asking the questions, but also it is my duty to do so because she put -- she said here that somebody savagely shot at Kosevo Hospital. And I spent 50 years of my life working in Kosevo Hospital and training there, and it's very dear to my heart, just as it is to Mrs. Zaimovic, but I have to demonstrate here the factual situation, what the facts were. In that hospital compound there were tanks and artillery pieces and brigades. There were criminals named -- one of them was named Kinez, the Chinaman because he was a very powerful man in that hospital. So the hospital was everything but a hospital. Quite simply, there was a lot of armed force there. They abused the traumatology ward and the entire compound, the faculty. They shot there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you can put as many questions as you wish to the witness, and you are entitled to put your case, but you are bound by the answer given by the witness. So you do not have to put every point to the witness, and then there's no need to deal with all of these documents. You can deal with it to test the credibility, one or two or several points of such nature, and then you can proceed. Putting every point to the witness, in the Chamber's view, is a waste of time. Ms. Sutherland, what do you -- would you say to this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour, although I note that the stamp hasn't been translated, but apart from that it has.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. In the same line, it will be marked for identification pending translation as 1D127.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be MFI D127.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's proceed, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mrs. Zaimovic, I'm going to put my case to you and make an assertion, and I'd like to see your answer. The Kosevo Hospital was a torture place for the Serbs; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have 1D947 next, please. And while we're waiting, did you know Mr. Vladimir Kojovic.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: On the basis of this document -- well, this part here where it says: "We have also learned that Dr. --" Actually, the previous one in Serbian. "We also found out that Dr. Vladimir Kojovic, who works in the Kosevo Hospital mistreated Serbs in his very own way and that Nedeljka Simic, a doctor of the same hospital helped the Serbs and shielded them --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] translation doesn't correspond with the B/C/S document. The B/C/S document is dated the 28th of July and the English translation is 18th of June, 1994, and the other one is 1993 in July.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Serbian version was not placed there, 947. This is the old Serbian document -- the old document, I mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you try 1D947. I was advise this is the correct document, so shall we proceed in the absence of the English translation for the moment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This is the previous document. This is 946. Let's have a look now. Yes. This is 946. We are actually asking for 947 to be called up. We can also have it placed on the ELMO, the Serbian version. The mistake is in e-court obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So the reference here is to a Serb who is mistreating Serbs at the Kosevo Hospital, and Dr. Nedeljka Simic is protecting them and giving them shelter. Have you heard of that doctor Nedeljka Simic?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Ms. Sutherland, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. The document on the left and the right of the screen are exactly the same, and it's -- it's document 1D946 and 1D947. It's the same document. So we don't have even the B/C/S of the document that Mr. Karadzic is reading from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. There seems to be a mistake on the -- on the Defence part. Let's proceed. Let's move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll deal with it tomorrow perhaps. Then could I have document 949, please. At least the relevant portions have been translated. So we have the document now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The date is the 8th of May, 1995. The Muslim intentions in the area of Sarajevo. This is intelligence, so it is confidential information again. That: "The MUP of Republika Srpska, RDB, through operative activities has received information that plans for attacks at Sarajevo have been prepared and finalised. Four brigades have been brought to Sarajevo and three more expected from the area of Zenica. The attack is supposed to occur in several directions simultaneously." I apologise. I have to read this more slowly. "The attack should begin from the city," et cetera. Mrs. Zaimovic, do you know that in the summer of 1995, the Muslim army had started a large-scale offensive from the city and from Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know. I don't know anything about any of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Let us move on to paragraph 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. 5: "An 82-millimetre battery is located in the new maternity building, and they are occasionally taken out the main side entrance towards the stadium. Two mountain cannons, B1, are located on the premises of the Kosevo Hospital, in the part near the faculty of civil engineering." Do you know that there were two mountain cannons in -- on the premises of the Kosevo Hospital?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But they were firing. Did you hear the explosions?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: No. In my opinion, that was certainly not the case. These are your reports. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Let us move on to the next paragraph and then the last sentence in that next paragraph. "The sniper nest is above the school for deaf mutes." Nemanja Vlatkovic was the name of the school, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. That's what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we move on to the next page, please. The second paragraph on the next page: "The command of the 2nd SMB is at the faculty of civilian engineering and headquarters is at the institute of geology in the building of the hygiene institute. The civil engineering faculty is right next to the hospital." You did you mark it; right?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Are you saying that this did not actually happen?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: What is it that you think? What is it that I'm claiming? I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is it your assertion that these military installations were not in the localities specified in this document?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Do you understand what I'm saying to you, that about these military things that you're talking about in the city, I have no idea about that. You keep putting these questions to me, and I have no idea about any of that that you're asking me about. Do you understand that I don't know anything about this? I wasn't interested in it at all. I was doing completely different things.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mrs. Zaimovic, you said several times here that Serbs were firing at the city. So now we have to see whether they were firing at legitimate targets or whether they were randomly shooting all over town. Do you agree that there is a difference, if there is a cannon, a howitzer, a mortar at Biljevina, doesn't that make a difference? Does it make the situation different if there was not a mortar battery there or howitzers or whatever?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you know full well what you did. You know that you surrounded Sarajevo. You know that you fired whenever you wanted to. You killed people whenever you wanted to. People had to get organised and defend themselves. But I don't know about these military targets at all. I don't know about this kind of thing at all. You have to understand that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour, but again the stamp hasn't been translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If I can get the confirmation from the Court Officer that this -- this -- these kind of documents will be translated officially by the CLSS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: They will be marked for identification pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D128, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, having followed the evidence of Mrs. Zaimovic so far, I don't think there's a point of you continuing to put those documents relating to the locations of ABiH, et cetera. You can put your case, and then you have another opportunity to prove what you put to the witness, but given the position of the witness that she does not know anything about military location or the attack from the BiH Army, I don't think it's -- it will help your case at this moment. So I -- I tell you to move on your different topic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, we are getting closer and closer to the hospital. As for the rest of today and tomorrow, we are going to be dealing with what it was that happened in that hospital that Mrs. Zaimovic portrayed as an innocent target. We are going to prove that that was not the case at all, and you will see that the situation was quite different to what Mrs. Zaimovic has been saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As I tell you, Mr. Karadzic, put your case and then move on to another topic. You don't have to deal with all these documents with this witness. You will have another opportunity.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D950, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mrs. Zaimovic, what about the salaries of Serbs and Muslims in Kosevo Hospital? Were they the same?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't have any salaries at all at the beginning of the war. The salaries had always been the same, whenever we received them, that is. There was no difference whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We'll deal with that later. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the third paragraph in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: According to the information we have received, there is a very small number of people of Serb ethnicity admitted to the Kosevo Hospital, those being the ones whose bare lives to be rescued by doctors' interventions only. After the first signs of recovery, executioners enter the rooms. They beat the Serb patients, returning them to a devastating situation. In relation to that, the source states that a certain Mirza employed as a security guard in the hospital, as well as Senada, a nurse, and a medical technician, Almir, are the people who terrorise the Serbs in the Kosevo Hospital the most. On the 31th of December, 1992, the three of them placed all Serbs who were on the ward in one room, in which, on the morning of the 1st of January, 1993, a group of soldiers of the so-called BiH Army barged into the room beating the patients mercilessly and torturing them for two or three hours. A certain Marinkovic had died from the beating. Are you saying that this did not happen?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about this, but I assert that no such thing every happened at the hospital. Everybody was treated the same way, really and truly. These are pure fabrications.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know these persons whose names were mentioned?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document, Your Excellencies. All of these reports are strictly confidential or were strictly confidential when they were created.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Same position, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: They will be marked for identification pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D129.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could I have 1D951, please. 1D951. It is possible that there is no translation yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I think you didn't understand me in full. I just asked you to put all of your case to the witness and move on to other topics instead of showing all the documents about which the witness has no knowledge at all. There's no point of continuing such practice. Put all the case. And having received the answer, you proceed to ask other topics.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, but this is an opportunity, because it has to do with the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Madam, let me put it this way: Do you know that gunpowder was smuggled in the oxygen bottles that were sent to you in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. How could I know that kind of thing?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Well, that was rather well known. It was written about in the media.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I have not read about that, and I have no way of knowing about that really.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to move on to another topic, namely what happened to your colleagues in the Kosevo Hospital. Now I'm going to ask -- actually, 951 is a document I wanted to tender as well. It is another secret report at the time when the smuggling was uncovered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, apart from the principle we've taken as regards the admissibility of documents, given our -- given my instruction to move on to another topic without relying on such documents, the Chamber will not admit this document. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mrs. Zaimovic, in your statement of the 9th of April, 2000, you say on page 00938863, paragraph 4, that Serb and Croat doctors stayed on, for the most part, but that then, slowly, they started leaving one by one. Is that the way you had put it?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. At first the doctors were there with us for the most part, and as time went by, Serbs and Croats were leaving us and ultimately some Muslims as well whose families had left town. Masses of people had left town because they were afraid for their lives. So out of a total of 14 doctors, we ultimately had only two, one Muslim and one Croat.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you trying to say that they were leaving because they felt good and safe and that they went to the Serb side and gave us statements as to what happened to them in Kosevo Hospital; or are you going to accept that they were threatened there, primarily Serbs and Jews and Croats, and that they fled to our side and then gave statements to us?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: In Sarajevo, nobody was threatened really, especially not at the Kosevo Hospital. They worked together with us side by side. We shared the very last bits of food that we had. Ethnic Serbs were the first to leave our clinic, then Croats with their families as the war became more and more intensive. They all had young children, et cetera, and finally Muslim doctors left. I repeat: We only had two doctors left who taught young doctors how they could work and help as well. You can imagine what it was like for us to operate in that situation with so few doctors around. You know full well what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Are you trying to say, Mrs. Zaimovic, that a doctor who tries to leave town without permission was not punished and was not sentenced to a prison term of half a year, at least?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean prison sentence. You are a doctor and you killed patients. You took the oath and you did horrible things. What do you know? You should read up on this. Doctors who left went to save their lives. Some went to your side, and others went just to save themselves and their families, like all citizens of Sarajevo. Sarajevo was a city under siege, terrible siege. So many days and so many shells fell. Everybody was in fear for their families and themselves. It was very hard to live in town, and you know that full well. You are taunting me with all these questions, but go on. I can take it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mrs. Zaimovic, I understand how you feel, and you are very -- you are in a very difficult situation, but please try to answer the question. By that way you are assisting the Chamber. You are not answering to Mr. Karadzic but to the Chamber. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I apologise, Your Excellency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, you don't have to apologise. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me whether you knew Dr. Kemal Drndo.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was an excellent surgeon.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And an excellent man, too.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, an excellent man and excellent surgeon.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And he was professor to me and to your husband. Now, can you tell me why he was replaced?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: He wasn't replaced at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And what post was he when the end of the war came?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: He was the principal surgeon of the emergency ward.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But wasn't he a director before that?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: He was the principle surgeon at the emergency ward.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And what was he at the beginning of the war?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: He was the head of thoracic surgery.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did you know Professor Najdanovic, who was also at the thoracic surgery ward?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mrs. Zaimovic, I have to doubt that, because it's common knowledge what happened to him. So I can't believe it when you say you don't know what happened to him.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what happened to him. All I know is that he was killed. That's all I know, but I don't know what actually happened to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know that there are photographs of him stark naked and circumcised and being led through your hospital compound and then they killed him and threw him into a rubbish dump, into a container? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't. I really don't.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I have 1D911, next, please. 1D911 is the number of the next document I'd like called up on e-court, please. We have the Serbian version there. The date is the 17th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, does that document contain the contents that you just put to the witness? That being the case, recommend you to move on to your next topic. I said to you to put all the cases without having to rely on the documents. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Excellency, then I have to change my approach, and I cannot accept having the witness avoid matters that were so drastic that the whole of Sarajevo knew about them. I just can't believe that the witness is being sincere. It's -- it's a matter of confirming facts that everybody in town knew about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, as I told you, you can put all your case to the witness, and even you can ask whether -- to the witness whether she's lying or not, and then you'll have another opportunity to tender and prove the facts as you wish. As Judge Morrison told you, you should be bound by what the witness said in relation to her evidence. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Her testimony contains a lot of allegations about Serb conduct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, madam, you said that you knew Dr. Starovic. Do you know that on the 6th of April, at the very beginning of the war, when he was getting into his car, a neighbour of his who was an underage person shot at him with the intention of killing him?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know that. I know that Dr. Starovic fell ill, and because of his illness he left town.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do you know who Bane Surbat, a national hero is?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I have heard the name, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did you know his brother, Dr. Gojko Surbat?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Everybody living in Sarajevo knew Dr. Surbat. Do you know he was killed in front of his own house?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know that, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And what about Dr. Vladimir Belenki, have you heard of him? He was a doctor at the ear, nose, and mouth department.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I have heard of Dr. Vladimir Belenki from that department, but I don't know what happened to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: He was killed too. Now, have you heard of Dr. Zarko Mijatovic, who worked in the maternity ward and helped all the women of Sarajevo give birth?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And do you know that he was wounded through a firearm?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, do you know how many other doctors and nurses were wounded and injured in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm asking about a man who was wounded by the Green Berets with the intention of killing him.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know that he was wounded and injured. I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did you know Dr. Mihajlo Vujovic.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know that he was stabbed in the stomach a number of times and hanged at his own threshold with the intention of making it look like a suicide?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know, and I think that that is something that should be proved. I have -- I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know Dr. Bajko Hogic [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Of course I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know that the doctors who returned to work after those first clashes and conflicts, that he would say to them at meetings, What are you doing here, and how dare you address me, and that's how he sent doctors packing?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that, but I know that he was an excellent boss and an excellent neuro surgeon. And he did very hard work in the clinical centre when he lost a lot of doctors and he had to work overtime. Certainly he would be angry with people from time to time, but he was a real doctor, a real humanist, and, out of respect, everybody should get up when he comes into a room.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And do you know when they offered him to become part of a peace mission he said, What peace mission? We've been waiting for this from 1804, which was the first Serbian -- the date of the first Serbian uprising?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: No. I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you mean to say, Mrs. Zaimovic, that Dr. Dejan Kafka, from a Serbian Jewish marriage, a fateful marriage, and Dr. Marko Vukovic, Dr. Sabljak and Dr. Medenica and Veljko Nemanja, did not get a six-month sentence when they tried to leave?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you about Dejan Kafka. He was a doctor working at my clinic. He was married to a wonderful woman. His wife was really a wonderful woman. I don't know what ethnicity she was. But during the war, a son was born to him and we would all take presents to him, to help him out, clothing and firewood, and so on. And at one point, he felt that he could no longer remain at the clinic. He had to leave. He collected up his belongings because his wife had gone to Belgrade before him and he escaped through the tunnel. Now, what happened to him after that I don't know, but he worked at our clinic for a long time because his father was the first head of the surgical ward, Professor Dr. Ivan Kafka, who was an exceptional surgeon and with whom I worked for many years.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Dr. Kafka, yes, his father was very well known and his mother was a Serb woman and his father was a Jew. But all the ones that I listed we see were given six-month prison sentences because they attempted to leave town?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA ZAIMOVIC
